title: RANT: Discipline & work ethic are NOT genetic traits!
summary: Attacks the resurging YouTube-fitness idea that discipline, motivation and mental toughness are genetically predetermined. Looks, height and disease are largely genetic, but strength of mind is built through upbringing, environment and effort. He argues genetics talk serves only to flatter the gifted and discourage the rest, that enhanced influencers claiming innate drive are hypocrites, and that humans choose their path.

claims.claim: The idea that mental toughness, discipline and motivation are genetic traits fixed at birth is the worst case of determinism; it implies you must be born a winner to be one.
Looks, height and not having a fatal disease are largely genetic, but strength of mind, will and determination are 100% built, shaped by culture and the cards dealt in childhood.
Education, environment, schooling and people who push you to read influence whether you're considered smart far more than birth, except for genuine malformations; the same holds for gym drive.
No 'discipline gene' has ever been proven, even by those who claim to rely heavily on science.
No one is born a champion bodybuilder; good genetics without applying yourself produce nothing.
He knows guys with far better genetics (insertions, hormones, fat distribution) who aren't a tenth of his level because they don't train; training is everything.

Genetics talk in YouTube fitness serves two purposes: making the gifted feel superior and making the less gifted feel bad; it is never used constructively (e.g. to guide diet or which body parts to prioritize).
Claiming innate superiority is like kings claiming divine right; there is no destiny or fate, your actions determine where you go.
Most influencers pushing this idea were once weak and small like everyone else.
Wanting to be big and strong is already the motivation you need; you don't need 'motivation DNA'.
He wasn't motivated at 13-14; he had to find motivation, and the more he worked on himself the more it grew until it became part of him, a discipline he nourished.
Influencers with young male audiences who say they were 'born champions' teach that hard work does nothing, and fans then cope with excuses like bad genetics or not being 'born disciplined'.
No one is born disciplined; some parents teach it, but even without that (he didn't get it for sports) it can be found in every person.
Enhanced influencers claiming innate drive are hypocrites: hormones make them feel motivated, and without them they'd fall into deep depression within a month.
Humans have the most freedom of any species; if we fail it's on us, and lacking the right genes is no excuse because you can still make the most of what you have.
He believes the natural limit does not exist.
